<security_assessment>

<details>
This is a standard systemd unit file describing a D-Bus notification service. The only executable line of note is `ExecCondition=/bin/sh -c '[ -n "$WAYLAND_DISPLAY" ]'`, which simply checks whether the environment variable `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is non-empty—a common, benign heuristic for deciding whether to run under Wayland or X11. There is no `eval`, no encoded commands, no network requests, no file system tampering, and no suspicious external calls. The service entrypoint (`/usr/bin/hokum service`) is the expected executable for a notification daemon. While the absence of checksummed sources does not by itself indicate malice, it is also a common practice for systemd units shipped via AUR packages and does not warrant an unsafe classification per the stated rubric.
</details>

The sources are clearly defined and appear to be part of normal packaging workflow. Consequently, the file is safe from a supply‑chain perspective, though the checksum mismatch is a packaging error that should be corrected.
